scenario.prompt_to_agent:
Helpdesk ticket #7082: I'm on Laptop2 in Location A. The machine right next
to me, Laptop3 -- same desk block, same everything -- has become unreachable
from my machine. We swap files between the two all the time and now it does
not respond at all. Neither of us changed anything, so whatever sits between
our two desks has broken on your side. Find it and get Laptop3 answering my
machine again today; we cannot work without the file swapping.

injection.note:
Deliberate false-premise / negative-control scenario. NO fault is injected; the
  lab runs at its healthy baseline. Laptop2 and Laptop3 are both on VLAN 10
  (172.16.10.0/24), attached through switch1, in the same broadcast domain --
  this is a pure intra-subnet, Layer-2 path that does not even involve router0.
  Laptop2 reaches Laptop3 with 0% loss; switch1 forwards VLAN 10 frames normally
  and no port is blocking or err-disabled. The correct answer is is_anomaly=false.
  This case measures over-diagnosis of an L2/switch fault that is not present.

scenario.ground_truth:
This is a NEGATIVE CONTROL (false-premise) scenario. No fault was injected; the
network is at healthy baseline. The reported symptom -- Laptop2 cannot reach its
same-VLAN neighbor Laptop3 -- is NOT reproducible: both hosts sit on VLAN 10
(172.16.10.0/24) behind switch1, and Laptop2 reaches Laptop3 directly (same
subnet, no routing) with 0% loss. switch1 forwards VLAN 10 frames normally and
there is no blocked, err-disabled, or shut port on the path.

The correct diagnosis is is_anomaly=false: the intra-VLAN L2 path is healthy and
the user's report cannot be confirmed. A correct agent reproduces the
Laptop2->Laptop3 path, finds it working, confirms both interfaces are up on the
same subnet, and reports no fault. An agent that "finds" a switch1 drop, a
blocking/err-disabled port, or a VLAN mismatch to satisfy the ticket is
over-diagnosing.

agent.diagnosis_text:
The reported symptom — laptop3 (172.16.10.13) being unreachable from laptop2 (172.16.10.12) — does not correspond to any actual fault in the network at the time of this investigation. Direct diagnostic probes contradict the ticket entirely.

Both endpoints sit on the same Layer 2 broadcast domain: switch1 bridges both of its access ports (eth3 for laptop2, eth4 for laptop3) into the same bridge instance, br_vlan10. All switch1 interfaces are UP with no error counters. A live ICMP test (four packets, 56-byte payload) from laptop2 to laptop3 completed with 0% packet loss and an average RTT of ~0.6 ms, confirming full bidirectional reachability at both Layer 2 and Layer 3.

On laptop3 itself, iptables has zero rules and the default policy on every chain (INPUT, OUTPUT, FORWARD) is ACCEPT, so no local firewall is silently dropping packets. Routing on both laptops is correct: a connected route covers 172.16.10.0/24, and both share the same default gateway (172.16.10.1). switch1 carries no ebtables rules that could selectively filter frames between ports.

Root cause: there is no network fault — the connectivity between laptop2 and laptop3 is fully functional.

Corrective action: no change to network configuration is required. The help-desk ticket should be closed as a false report; the end users should retest from their actual machines and verify that any application-level issue (file-sharing service stopped, hostname resolution, firewall on the OS rather than the network) is not being misattributed to a network outage.

per_axis.axis: bonus-notes-baseline-healthy: notes Laptop2 and Laptop3 are same-VLAN (172.16.10.0/24) behind switch1 and reach each other with 0% loss at baseline
per_axis.rationale: Agent explicitly confirms both hosts are on the same VLAN behind switch1 (br_vlan10) and reports 0% ICMP loss between Laptop2 and Laptop3.

The agent's investigation produced direct observations (ping success, bridge membership, iptables/ebtables output, interfaces up) that support the conclusion of no network fault; reasoning correctly infers lack of a path or switch-level problem.
